(after [[:en:Gaston Maspero|Gaston Maspero]], 1907) }} The '''[[:en:Egyptian sun temple|Egyptian sun temple]] of Niuserre''' is an '''Ancient Egyptian''' temple complex from the '''[[:en:Fifth Dynasty of Egypt|Fifth Dynasty of Egypt]]''', built by the Pharaoh '''[[:en:Nyuserre Ini|Niuserre Ini]]''' at '''[[:en:Abu Gorab|Abu Ghurab]]''', who ruled from approximately '''2455 to 2420 BCE'''.Chronology according to [[:en:Thomas Schneider|Thomas Schneider (Egyptologist)]]: ''Lexikon der Pharaonen.'' Albatros, Düsseldorf 2002, ISBN 3-491-96053-3. == '''History of Research''' == [[File:Abusir map.png|thumb|Overview of '''Abusir''', with the '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''' (top left)]] The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''' was first mentioned in the '''''[[:en:Description de l'Égypte|Description de l'Égypte]]''''', though at that time it was mistakenly identified as a '''[[:en:Pyramid|Pyramid]]'''. Because of this error, the structure was initially known as the '''"Pyramid of Righa."''' * '''1838''': '''[[:en:John Shae Perring|John Shae Perring]]''' attempted to excavate the supposed '''pyramid''', but only found remnants of the '''granite base'''. However, reliefs depicting a '''[[:en:Sed festival|Sed festival]]''' were discovered, sparking interest in further exploration. * '''1842''': Members of the '''{{ill|Prussian expedition to Egypt|de|Preußische Expedition nach Ägypten|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prussian expedition to Egypt|qq=|WD=Q20181134}}''', led by '''[[:en:Karl Richard Lepsius|Karl Richard Lepsius]]''', conducted precise measurements and listed the site as '''"XV"''' in the '''[[:en:Lepsius list of pyramids|Lepsius list of pyramids]]'''. * '''1882''': '''[[:en:Auguste Mariette|Auguste Mariette]]''' may have conducted a '''test excavation''', though no official records exist. * '''1882/83''': '''{{ill|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|de|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|qq=|WD=Q5729559}}''' uncovered '''ten alabaster basins''' and the '''alabaster altar'''. * '''1898–1901''': '''[[:en:Ludwig Borchardt|Ludwig Borchardt]]''' and '''{{ill|Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|de|Heinrich Schäfer (Ägyptologe)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|qq=|WD=Q98050}}''' fully excavated the site on behalf of the '''[[:en:Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft|German Oriental Society]]'''.{{Cite book |author=[[:en:Wolfgang Helck|Wolfgang Helck]] |editor=[[:en:Wolfgang Helck|Wolfgang Helck]] |title=Abu-Gurab |series={{ill|Lexicon of Egyptology|de|Lexikon der Ägyptologie|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lexicon of Egyptology|qq=|WD=Q1822307}} |volume=I |publisher=Harrassowitz |location=Wiesbaden |year=1975 |ISBN=3-447-01670-1 |pages=23}} Financial support was provided by '''[[:en:Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing|Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing]]'''. == '''Location and Significance''' == The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''', named '''''Šsp-jb-Rˁ''''' ("Pleasure of '''[[:en:Ra|Ra]]'''"), is located '''approximately 1.2 km northeast''' of the '''{{ill|Pyramids of Abusir|de|Pyramiden von Abusir|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pyramids of Abusir|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}'''. The '''Abusir necropolis''' is linked to the '''myth of Osiris''', in which '''[[:en:Osiris|Osiris]]''' was dismembered, and his body parts were scattered across different burial sites. The name '''"Abusir"''' derives from the Greek '''"Busiris"''', which itself comes from the Egyptian '''"Pr Wsjr"''' ("House of Osiris"). The '''solar temple''' was constructed on a natural hill, which was further elevated using artificial embankments. Beneath the structure, remains of '''older brick buildings''', possibly '''mastabas''', have been discovered. == '''The Solar Temple Complex''' == Unlike other '''temples''' dedicated to various deities, '''solar temples''' feature '''an open courtyard''', where a '''central altar''' and '''cult object''' stand in the open air. This contrasts with traditional '''Egyptian temples''', which were designed as enclosed sanctuaries housing the '''god's image'''. === '''Known Solar Temples''' === A total of '''eight solar temples''' are known from '''historical texts''', but only '''two''' have been '''excavated''': 1. '''Niuserre's Solar Temple''' (this site) 2. '''[[:en:Sun Temple of Userkaf|Solar Temple of Userkaf]]''' Other '''undiscovered''' solar temples belong to: * '''[[:en:Sahure|Sahure]]''' * '''[[:en:Neferirkare Kakai|Neferirkare Kakai]]''' * '''[[:en:Neferefre|Raneferef]]''' * '''[[:en:Menkauhor Kaiu|Menkauhor Kaiu]]''' === '''Architectural Inspiration''' === The design of '''solar temples''' follows the '''three-part layout''' of '''royal pyramid complexes''': 1. '''Valley Temple''' 2. '''Causeway''' 3. '''Upper Sanctuary on the Desert Plateau''' A '''large obelisk''' served as the '''focal point''' of the sanctuary, mirroring the '''pyramid''' in traditional '''royal complexes'''. === '''Possible Connections to Heliopolis''' === It is debated whether the '''{{ill|Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|de|Tempel des Re in Heliopolis|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}''' served as the '''prototype''' for '''solar temples'''. '''[[:en:Jochem Kahl|Jochem Kahl]]''' suggests that '''[[:en:Ra|Ra]]''' may have been '''worshiped as early as the Second Dynasty''', though his association with '''Heliopolis''' is not firmly attested until the '''Pyramid Texts''' at the end of the '''Fifth Dynasty'''. == '''Key Structures''' == * '''Valley Temple''': Served as the '''entrance''' to the '''causeway'''. * '''Causeway''': A '''100-meter-long sloped ramp''' connecting the '''Valley Temple''' to the '''Upper Temple'''. * '''Obelisk''': The '''primary cult object''', likely '''37 meters tall'''. * '''Altar''': A '''circular alabaster slab''', surrounded by '''four hieroglyphic "ḥtp" blocks''' symbolizing '''offerings''' to '''Ra'''. * '''Great and Small Slaughterhouses''': Featured '''alabaster basins''', likely for '''ritual purification''' rather than actual '''animal slaughter'''. * '''Solar Barque''': A '''20-meter-long brick structure''', imitating the '''mythological boat of Ra'''. == '''Function and Religious Role''' == The '''temple cult''' was dedicated to '''Ra, Hathor''', and the '''Pharaoh''', with a '''priesthood''' ensuring ritual maintenance. The complex emphasized '''Ra's role as the creator''', featuring elaborate '''seasonal reliefs''' that '''depicted natural cycles''': * '''Animal reproduction''' * '''Fish migration in the Nile''' * '''Arrival of birds in the Delta''' * '''Harvesting of flax, honey, and figs''' This '''imagery reinforced the concept of eternal renewal''', both in '''nature''' and '''kingship'''. == '''Further Reading''' == {{Cite book |author=[[:en:Miroslav Verner|Miroslav Verner]] |title=The Pyramids: The Mystery, Culture, and Science of Egypt's Great Monuments |publisher=Rowohlt |year=1998 |ISBN=3-498-07062-2}} {{Navigation Solar Temples of the Fifth Dynasty}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Ancient Egyptian temples]] }} [[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Abusir]] [[Category:Ra]] [[Category:Sonnenheiligtum der 5. Egypt|de|Preußische Expedition nach Ägypten|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prussian expedition to Egypt|qq=|WD=Q20181134}}''', led by '''[[:en:Karl Richard Lepsius|Karl Richard Lepsius]]''', conducted precise measurements and listed the site as '''"XV"''' in the '''[[:en:Lepsius list of pyramids|Lepsius list of pyramids]]'''. * '''1882''': '''[[:en:Auguste Mariette|Auguste Mariette]]''' may have conducted a '''test excavation''', though no official records exist. * '''1882/83''': '''{{ill|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|de|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|qq=|WD=Q5729559}}''' uncovered '''ten alabaster basins''' and the '''alabaster altar'''. * '''1898–1901''': '''[[:en:Ludwig Borchardt|Ludwig Borchardt]]''' and '''{{ill|Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|de|Heinrich Schäfer (Ägyptologe)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|qq=|WD=Q98050}}''' fully excavated the site on behalf of the '''[[:en:Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft|German Oriental Society]]'''.{{Cite book |author=[[:en:Wolfgang Helck|Wolfgang Helck]] |editor=[[:en:Wolfgang Helck|Wolfgang Helck]] |title=Abu-Gurab |series={{ill|Lexicon of Egyptology|de|Lexikon der Ägyptologie|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lexicon of Egyptology|qq=|WD=Q1822307}} |volume=I |publisher=Harrassowitz |location=Wiesbaden |year=1975 |ISBN=3-447-01670-1 |pages=23}} Financial support was provided by '''[[:en:Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing|Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing]]'''. == '''Location and Significance''' == The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''', named '''''Šsp-jb-Rˁ''''' ("Pleasure of '''[[:en:Ra|Ra]]'''"), is located '''approximately 1.2 km northeast''' of the '''{{ill|Pyramids of Abusir|de|Pyramiden von Abusir|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pyramids of Abusir|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}'''. The '''Abusir necropolis''' is linked to the '''myth of Osiris''', in which '''[[:en:Osiris|Osiris]]''' was dismembered, and his body parts were scattered across different burial sites. The name '''"Abusir"''' derives from the Greek '''"Busiris"''', which itself comes from the Egyptian '''"Pr Wsjr"''' ("House of Osiris"). The '''solar temple''' was constructed on a natural hill, which was further elevated using artificial embankments. Beneath the structure, remains of '''older brick buildings''', possibly '''mastabas''', have been discovered. == '''The Solar Temple Complex''' == Unlike other '''temples''' dedicated to various deities, '''solar temples''' feature '''an open courtyard''', where a '''central altar''' and '''cult object''' stand in the open air. This contrasts with traditional '''Egyptian temples''', which were designed as enclosed sanctuaries housing the '''god's image'''. === '''Known Solar Temples''' === A total of '''eight solar temples''' are known from '''historical texts''', but only '''two''' have been '''excavated''': 1. '''Niuserre's Solar Temple''' (this site) 2. '''[[:en:Sun Temple of Userkaf|Solar Temple of Userkaf]]''' Other '''undiscovered''' solar temples belong to: * '''[[:en:Sahure|Sahure]]''' * '''[[:en:Neferirkare Kakai|Neferirkare Kakai]]''' * '''[[:en:Neferefre|Raneferef]]''' * '''[[:en:Menkauhor Kaiu|Menkauhor Kaiu]]''' === '''Architectural Inspiration''' === The design of '''solar temples''' follows the '''three-part layout''' of '''royal pyramid complexes''': 1. '''Valley Temple''' 2. '''Causeway''' 3. '''Upper Sanctuary on the Desert Plateau''' A '''large obelisk''' served as the '''focal point''' of the sanctuary, mirroring the '''pyramid''' in traditional '''royal complexes'''. === '''Possible Connections to Heliopolis''' === It is debated whether the '''{{ill|Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|de|Tempel des Re in Heliopolis|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}''' served as the '''prototype''' for '''solar temples'''. '''[[:en:Jochem Kahl|Jochem Kahl]]''' suggests that '''[[:en:Ra|Ra]]''' may have been '''worshiped as early as the Second Dynasty''', though his association with '''Heliopolis''' is not firmly attested until the '''Pyramid Texts''' at the end of the '''Fifth Dynasty'''. == '''Key Structures''' == * '''Valley Temple''': Served as the '''entrance''' to the '''causeway'''. * '''Causeway''': A '''100-meter-long sloped ramp''' connecting the '''Valley Temple''' to the '''Upper Temple'''. * '''Obelisk''': The '''primary cult object''', likely '''37 meters tall'''. * '''Altar''': A '''circular alabaster slab''', surrounded by '''four hieroglyphic "ḥtp" blocks''' symbolizing '''offerings''' to '''Ra'''. * '''Great and Small Slaughterhouses''': Featured '''alabaster basins''', likely for '''ritual purification''' rather than actual '''animal slaughter'''. * '''Solar Barque''': A '''20-meter-long brick structure''', imitating the '''mythological boat of Ra'''. == '''Function and Religious Role''' == The '''temple cult''' was dedicated to '''Ra, Hathor''', and the '''Pharaoh''', with a '''priesthood''' ensuring ritual maintenance. The complex emphasized '''Ra's role as the creator''', featuring elaborate '''seasonal reliefs''' that '''depicted natural cycles''': * '''Animal reproduction''' * '''Fish migration in the Nile''' * '''Arrival of birds in the Delta''' * '''Harvesting of flax, honey, and figs''' This '''imagery reinforced the concept of eternal renewal''', both in '''nature''' and '''kingship'''. == '''Further Reading''' == {{Cite book |author=[[:en:Miroslav Verner|Miroslav Verner]] |title=The Pyramids: The Mystery, Culture, and Science of Egypt's Great Monuments |publisher=Rowohlt |year=1998 |ISBN=3-498-07062-2}} {{Navigation Solar Temples of the Fifth Dynasty}} {{draft categories| }} [[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]] [[ar:معبد ني وسر رع]] [[arz:معبد الشمس نى-اوسر-رع]] {{Commons category|Nyuserre sun temple}} [[fr:Temple solaire d'Abou Ghorab]] [[nl:Zonnetempel van Nioeserre]] [[sk:Niuserreho slnečný chrám]] {{translated page|de|Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre|version=249954049|comment=Imported full de history}} {{wikidata link|Q2009417}} [[Category:Abusir]] [[Category:Ancient Egyptian temples]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Pages without valid translation templates or en interwikis]] [[Category:Ra]] [[Category:Sonnenheiligtum der 5. [[ar:معبد ني وسر رع]][[arz:معبد الشمس نى-اوسر-رع]][[commons:Category:Nyuserre sun temple]][[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]][[fr:Temple solaire d'Abou Ghorab]][[nl:Zonnetempel van Nioeserre]][[sk:Niuserreho slnečný chrám]][[ur:معبد نی اوسررع]] [[ar:معبد ني وسر رع]][[arz:معبد الشمس نى-اوسر-رع]][[commons:Category:Nyuserre sun temple]][[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]][[fr:Temple solaire d'Abou Ghorab]][[nl:Zonnetempel van Nioeserre]][[sk:Niuserreho slnečný chrám]][[ur:معبد نی اوسررع]] [[ar:معبد ني وسر رع]][[arz:معبد الشمس نى-اوسر-رع]][[sn:commons:Category:Nyuserre sun temple]][[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]][[fr:Temple solaire d'Abou Ghorab]][[nl:Zonnetempel van Nioeserre]][[sk:Niuserreho slnečný chrám]][[ur:معبد نی اوسررع]] {{Infobox hieroglyphs |NAME = ra-O42:ib-O25
Schesep-ib-Re
''Šsp-jb-Rˁ''
''Pleasure Place of [[:en:Ra|Ra]]'' |IMAGE1 = Temple-solaire-abousir.jpg |IMAGE1-WIDTH = 300px |IMAGE1-CAPTION = Reconstruction of the '''Solar Temple of Niuserre'''
(after [[:en:Gaston Maspero|Gaston Maspero]], 1907) }} The '''[[:en:Egyptian sun temple|Egyptian sun temple]] of Niuserre''' is an '''Ancient Egyptian''' temple complex from the '''[[:en:Fifth Dynasty of Egypt|Fifth Dynasty of Egypt]]''', built by the Pharaoh '''[[:en:Nyuserre Ini|Niuserre Ini]]''' at '''[[:en:Abu Gorab|Abu Ghurab]]''', who ruled from approximately '''2455 to 2420 BCE'''.Chronology according to [[:en:Thomas Schneider|Thomas Schneider (Egyptologist)]]: ''Lexikon der Pharaonen.'' Albatros, Düsseldorf 2002, ISBN 3-491-96053-3. == '''History of Research''' == [[File:Abusir map.png|thumb|Overview of '''Abusir''', with the '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''' (top left)]] The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''' was first mentioned in the '''''[[:en:Description de l'Égypte|Description de l'Égypte]]''''', though at that time it was mistakenly identified as a '''[[:en:Pyramid|Pyramid]]'''. Because of this error, the structure was initially known as the '''"Pyramid of Righa."''' * '''1838''': '''[[:en:John Shae Perring|John Shae Perring]]''' attempted to excavate the supposed '''pyramid''', but only found remnants of the '''granite base'''. However, reliefs depicting a '''[[:en:Sed festival|Sed festival]]''' were discovered, sparking interest in further exploration. * '''1842''': Members of the '''{{ill|Prussian expedition to Egypt|de|Preußische Expedition nach Ägypten|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prussian expedition to Egypt|qq=|WD=Q20181134}}''', led by '''[[:en:Karl Richard Lepsius|Karl Richard Lepsius]]''', conducted precise measurements and listed the site as '''"XV"''' in the '''[[:en:Lepsius list of pyramids|Lepsius list of pyramids]]'''. * '''1882''': '''[[:en:Auguste Mariette|Auguste Mariette]]''' may have conducted a '''test excavation''', though no official records exist. * '''1882/83''': '''{{ill|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|de|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|qq=|WD=Q5729559}}''' uncovered '''ten alabaster basins''' and the '''alabaster altar'''. * '''1898–1901''': '''[[:en:Ludwig Borchardt|Ludwig Borchardt]]''' and '''{{ill|Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|de|Heinrich Schäfer (Ägyptologe)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|qq=|WD=Q98050}}''' fully excavated the site on behalf of the '''[[:en:Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft|German Oriental Society]]'''.{{Cite book |author=[[:en:Wolfgang Helck|Wolfgang Helck]] |editor=[[:en:Wolfgang Helck|Wolfgang Helck]] |title=Abu-Gurab |series={{ill|Lexicon of Egyptology|de|Lexikon der Ägyptologie|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lexicon of Egyptology|qq=|WD=Q1822307}} |volume=I |publisher=Harrassowitz |location=Wiesbaden |year=1975 |ISBN=3-447-01670-1 |pages=23}} Financial support was provided by '''[[:en:Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing|Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing]]'''. == '''Location and Significance''' == The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''', named '''''Šsp-jb-Rˁ''''' ("Pleasure of '''[[:en:Ra|Ra]]'''"), is located '''approximately 1.2 km northeast''' of the '''{{ill|Pyramids of Abusir|de|Pyramiden von Abusir|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pyramids of Abusir|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}'''. The '''Abusir necropolis''' is linked to the '''myth of Osiris''', in which '''[[:en:Osiris|Osiris]]''' was dismembered, and his body parts were scattered across different burial sites. The name '''"Abusir"''' derives from the Greek '''"Busiris"''', which itself comes from the Egyptian '''"Pr Wsjr"''' ("House of Osiris"). The '''solar temple''' was constructed on a natural hill, which was further elevated using artificial embankments. Beneath the structure, remains of '''older brick buildings''', possibly '''mastabas''', have been discovered. == '''The Solar Temple Complex''' == Unlike other '''temples''' dedicated to various deities, '''solar temples''' feature '''an open courtyard''', where a '''central altar''' and '''cult object''' stand in the open air. This contrasts with traditional '''Egyptian temples''', which were designed as enclosed sanctuaries housing the '''god's image'''. === '''Known Solar Temples''' === A total of '''eight solar temples''' are known from '''historical texts''', but only '''two''' have been '''excavated''': 1. '''Niuserre's Solar Temple''' (this site) 2. '''[[:en:Sun Temple of Userkaf|Solar Temple of Userkaf]]''' Other '''undiscovered''' solar temples belong to: * '''[[:en:Sahure|Sahure]]''' * '''[[:en:Neferirkare Kakai|Neferirkare Kakai]]''' * '''[[:en:Neferefre|Raneferef]]''' * '''[[:en:Menkauhor Kaiu|Menkauhor Kaiu]]''' === '''Architectural Inspiration''' === The design of '''solar temples''' follows the '''three-part layout''' of '''royal pyramid complexes''': 1. '''Valley Temple''' 2. '''Causeway''' 3. '''Upper Sanctuary on the Desert Plateau''' A '''large obelisk''' served as the '''focal point''' of the sanctuary, mirroring the '''pyramid''' in traditional '''royal complexes'''. === '''Possible Connections to Heliopolis''' === It is debated whether the '''{{ill|Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|de|Tempel des Re in Heliopolis|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}''' served as the '''prototype''' for '''solar temples'''. '''[[:en:Jochem Kahl|Jochem Kahl]]''' suggests that '''[[:en:Ra|Ra]]''' may have been '''worshiped as early as the Second Dynasty''', though his association with '''Heliopolis''' is not firmly attested until the '''Pyramid Texts''' at the end of the '''Fifth Dynasty'''. == '''Key Structures''' == * '''Valley Temple''': Served as the '''entrance''' to the '''causeway'''. * '''Causeway''': A '''100-meter-long sloped ramp''' connecting the '''Valley Temple''' to the '''Upper Temple'''. * '''Obelisk''': The '''primary cult object''', likely '''37 meters tall'''. * '''Altar''': A '''circular alabaster slab''', surrounded by '''four hieroglyphic "ḥtp" blocks''' symbolizing '''offerings''' to '''Ra'''. * '''Great and Small Slaughterhouses''': Featured '''alabaster basins''', likely for '''ritual purification''' rather than actual '''animal slaughter'''. * '''Solar Barque''': A '''20-meter-long brick structure''', imitating the '''mythological boat of Ra'''. == '''Function and Religious Role''' == The '''temple cult''' was dedicated to '''Ra, Hathor''', and the '''Pharaoh''', with a '''priesthood''' ensuring ritual maintenance. The complex emphasized '''Ra's role as the creator''', featuring elaborate '''seasonal reliefs''' that '''depicted natural cycles''': * '''Animal reproduction''' * '''Fish migration in the Nile''' * '''Arrival of birds in the Delta''' * '''Harvesting of flax, honey, and figs''' This '''imagery reinforced the concept of eternal renewal''', both in '''nature''' and '''kingship'''. == '''Further Reading''' == {{Cite book |author=[[:en:Miroslav Verner|Miroslav Verner]] |title=The Pyramids: The Mystery, Culture, and Science of Egypt's Great Monuments |publisher=Rowohlt |year=1998 |ISBN=3-498-07062-2}} {{Navigation Solar Temples of the Fifth Dynasty}} [[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]] [[ar:معبد ني وسر رع]] [[arz:معبد الشمس نى-اوسر-رع]] {{Commons category|Nyuserre sun temple}} [[fr:Temple solaire d'Abou Ghorab]] [[nl:Zonnetempel van Nioeserre]] [[sk:Niuserreho slnečný chrám]] {{translated page|de|Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre|version=249954049|comment=Imported full de history}} {{wikidata link|Q2009417}} [[Category:Abusir]] [[Category:Ancient Egyptian temples]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Pages without valid translation templates or en interwikis]] [[Category:Ra]] [[Category:Sonnenheiligtum der 5. Dynastie]] [[Category:Temples by person]] [[Category:Temples in Egypt]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Qq]]

Albatros, Düsseldorf 2002, ISBN 3-491-96053-3. == '''History of Research''' == [[File:Abusir map.png|thumb|Overview of '''Abusir''', with the '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''' (top left)]] The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''' was first mentioned in the '''''{{ill|Description de l'Égypte|en|Description de l'Égypte|WD=Q1200564|lt=Description de l'Égypte}}''''', though at that time it was mistakenly identified as a '''{{ill|Pyramid|en|Pyramid|WD=Q12516|lt=Pyramid}}'''. Because of this error, the structure was initially known as the '''"Pyramid of Righa."''' * '''1838''': '''{{ill|John Shae Perring|en|John Shae Perring|WD=Q382221|lt=John Shae Perring}}''' attempted to excavate the supposed '''pyramid''', but only found remnants of the '''granite base'''. However, reliefs depicting a '''{{ill|Sed festival|en|Sed festival|WD=Q604644|lt=Sed festival}}''' were discovered, sparking interest in further exploration. * '''1842''': Members of the '''{{ill|Prussian expedition to Egypt|de|Preußische Expedition nach Ägypten|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prussian expedition to Egypt|qq=|WD=Q20181134}}''', led by '''{{ill|Karl Richard Lepsius|en|Karl Richard Lepsius|WD=Q77231|lt=Karl Richard Lepsius}}''', conducted precise measurements and listed the site as '''"XV"''' in the '''{{ill|Lepsius list of pyramids|en|Lepsius list of pyramids|WD=Q224877|lt=Lepsius list of pyramids}}'''. * '''1882''': '''{{ill|Auguste Mariette|en|Auguste Mariette|WD=Q311850|lt=Auguste Mariette}}''' may have conducted a '''test excavation''', though no official records exist. * '''1882/83''': '''{{ill|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|de|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|qq=|WD=Q5729559}}''' uncovered '''ten alabaster basins''' and the '''alabaster altar'''. * '''1898–1901''': '''{{ill|Ludwig Borchardt|en|Ludwig Borchardt|WD=Q60758|lt=Ludwig Borchardt}}''' and '''{{ill|Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|de|Heinrich Schäfer (Ägyptologe)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|qq=|WD=Q98050}}''' fully excavated the site on behalf of the '''{{ill|Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft|en|Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft|WD=Q314420|lt=German Oriental Society}}'''.{{Cite book |author={{ill|Wolfgang Helck|en|Wolfgang Helck|WD=Q74888|lt=Wolfgang Helck}} |editor={{ill|Wolfgang Helck|en|Wolfgang Helck|WD=Q74888|lt=Wolfgang Helck}} |title=Abu-Gurab |series={{ill|Lexicon of Egyptology|de|Lexikon der Ägyptologie|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lexicon of Bissing|en|Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing|WD=Q121278|lt=Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing}}'''. == '''Location and Significance''' == The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''', named '''''Šsp-jb-Rˁ''''' ("Pleasure of '''{{ill|Ra|en|Ra|WD=Q1252904|lt=Ra}}'''"), is located '''approximately 1.2 km northeast''' of the '''{{ill|Pyramids of Abusir|de|Pyramiden von Abusir|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pyramids of Abusir|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}'''. Beneath the structure, remains of '''older brick buildings''', possibly '''mastabas''', have been discovered. == '''The Solar Temple Complex''' == Unlike other '''temples''' dedicated to various deities, '''solar temples''' feature '''an open courtyard''', where a '''central altar''' and '''cult object''' stand in the open air. This contrasts with traditional '''Egyptian temples''', which were designed as enclosed sanctuaries housing the '''god's image'''. === '''Known Solar Temples''' === A total of '''eight solar temples''' are known from '''historical texts''', but only '''two''' have been '''excavated''': 1. '''Niuserre's Solar Temple''' (this site) 2. '''{{ill|Sun Temple of Userkaf|en|Sun Temple of Userkaf|WD=Q2301943|lt=Solar Temple of Userkaf}}''' Other '''undiscovered''' solar temples belong to: * '''{{ill|Sahure|en|Sahure|WD=Q243692|lt=Sahure}}''' * '''{{ill|Neferirkare Kakai|en|Neferirkare Kakai|WD=Q268576|lt=Neferirkare Kakai}}''' * '''{{ill|Neferefre|en|Neferefre|WD=Q269271|lt=Raneferef}}''' * '''{{ill|Menkauhor Kaiu|en|Menkauhor Kaiu|WD=Q269257|lt=Menkauhor Kaiu}}''' === '''Architectural Inspiration''' === The design of '''solar temples''' follows the '''three-part layout''' of '''royal pyramid complexes''': 1. Schesep-ib-Re
''Šsp-jb-Rˁ''
''Pleasure Place of {{ill|Ra|en|Ra|WD=Q1252904|lt=Ra}}'' |IMAGE1 = Temple-solaire-abousir.jpg |IMAGE1-WIDTH = 300px |IMAGE1-CAPTION = Reconstruction of the '''Solar Temple of Niuserre'''
(after {{ill|Gaston Maspero|en|Gaston Maspero|WD=Q311816|lt=Gaston Maspero}}, 1907) }} The '''{{ill|Egyptian sun temple|en|Egyptian sun temple|WD=Q919238|lt=Egyptian sun temple}} of Niuserre''' is an '''Ancient Egyptian''' temple complex from the '''{{ill|Fifth Dynasty of Egypt|en|Fifth Dynasty of Egypt|WD=Q269237|lt=Fifth Dynasty of Egypt}}''', built by the Pharaoh '''{{ill|Nyuserre Ini|en|Nyuserre Ini|WD=Q269200|lt=Niuserre Ini}}''' at '''{{ill|Abu Gorab|en|Abu Gorab|WD=Q2038886|lt=Abu Ghurab}}''', who ruled from approximately '''2455 to 2420 BCE'''.Chronology according to {{ill|Thomas Schneider|en|Thomas Schneider|WD=Q1901973|lt=Thomas Schneider (Egyptologist)}}: ''Lexikon der Pharaonen.'' Albatros, Düsseldorf 2002, ISBN 3-491-96053-3. == '''History of Research''' == [[File:Abusir map.png|thumb|Overview of '''Abusir''', with the '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''' (top left)]] The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''' was first mentioned in the '''''{{ill|Description de l'Égypte|en|Description de l'Égypte|WD=Q1200564|lt=Description de l'Égypte}}''''', though at that time it was mistakenly identified as a '''{{ill|Pyramid|en|Pyramid|WD=Q12516|lt=Pyramid}}'''. Because of this error, the structure was initially known as the '''"Pyramid of Righa."''' * '''1838''': '''{{ill|John Shae Perring|en|John Shae Perring|WD=Q382221|lt=John Shae Perring}}''' attempted to excavate the supposed '''pyramid''', but only found remnants of the '''granite base'''. However, reliefs depicting a '''{{ill|Sed festival|en|Sed festival|WD=Q604644|lt=Sed festival}}''' were discovered, sparking interest in further exploration. * '''1842''': Members of the '''{{ill|Prussian expedition to Egypt|de|Preußische Expedition nach Ägypten|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prussian expedition to Egypt|qq=|WD=Q20181134}}''', led by '''{{ill|Karl Richard Lepsius|en|Karl Richard Lepsius|WD=Q77231|lt=Karl Richard Lepsius}}''', conducted precise measurements and listed the site as '''"XV"''' in the '''{{ill|Lepsius list of pyramids|en|Lepsius list of pyramids|WD=Q224877|lt=Lepsius list of pyramids}}'''. * '''1882''': '''{{ill|Auguste Mariette|en|Auguste Mariette|WD=Q311850|lt=Auguste Mariette}}''' may have conducted a '''test excavation''', though no official records exist. * '''1882/83''': '''{{ill|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|de|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|qq=|WD=Q5729559}}''' uncovered '''ten alabaster basins''' and the '''alabaster altar'''. * '''1898–1901''': '''{{ill|Ludwig Borchardt|en|Ludwig Borchardt|WD=Q60758|lt=Ludwig Borchardt}}''' and '''{{ill|Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|de|Heinrich Schäfer (Ägyptologe)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|qq=|WD=Q98050}}''' fully excavated the site on behalf of the '''{{ill|Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft|en|Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft|WD=Q314420|lt=German Oriental Society}}'''.{{Cite book |author={{ill|Wolfgang Helck|en|Wolfgang Helck|WD=Q74888|lt=Wolfgang Helck}} |editor={{ill|Wolfgang Helck|en|Wolfgang Helck|WD=Q74888|lt=Wolfgang Helck}} |title=Abu-Gurab |series={{ill|Lexicon of Egyptology|de|Lexikon der Ägyptologie|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lexicon of Egyptology|qq=|WD=Q1822307}} |volume=I |publisher=Harrassowitz |location=Wiesbaden |year=1975 |ISBN=3-447-01670-1 |pages=23}} Financial support was provided by '''{{ill|Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing|en|Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing|WD=Q121278|lt=Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing}}'''. == '''Location and Significance''' == The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''', named '''''Šsp-jb-Rˁ''''' ("Pleasure of '''{{ill|Ra|en|Ra|WD=Q1252904|lt=Ra}}'''"), is located '''approximately 1.2 km northeast''' of the '''{{ill|Pyramids of Abusir|de|Pyramiden von Abusir|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pyramids of Abusir|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}'''. The '''Abusir necropolis''' is linked to the '''myth of Osiris''', in which '''{{ill|Osiris|en|Osiris|WD=Q46491|lt=Osiris}}''' was dismembered, and his body parts were scattered across different burial sites. The name '''"Abusir"''' derives from the Greek '''"Busiris"''', which itself comes from the Egyptian '''"Pr Wsjr"''' ("House of Osiris"). The '''solar temple''' was constructed on a natural hill, which was further elevated using artificial embankments. Beneath the structure, remains of '''older brick buildings''', possibly '''mastabas''', have been discovered. == '''The Solar Temple Complex''' == Unlike other '''temples''' dedicated to various deities, '''solar temples''' feature '''an open courtyard''', where a '''central altar''' and '''cult object''' stand in the open air. This contrasts with traditional '''Egyptian temples''', which were designed as enclosed sanctuaries housing the '''god's image'''. === '''Known Solar Temples''' === A total of '''eight solar temples''' are known from '''historical texts''', but only '''two''' have been '''excavated''': 1. '''Niuserre's Solar Temple''' (this site) 2. '''{{ill|Sun Temple of Userkaf|en|Sun Temple of Userkaf|WD=Q2301943|lt=Solar Temple of Userkaf}}''' Other '''undiscovered''' solar temples belong to: * '''{{ill|Sahure|en|Sahure|WD=Q243692|lt=Sahure}}''' * '''{{ill|Neferirkare Kakai|en|Neferirkare Kakai|WD=Q268576|lt=Neferirkare Kakai}}''' * '''{{ill|Neferefre|en|Neferefre|WD=Q269271|lt=Raneferef}}''' * '''{{ill|Menkauhor Kaiu|en|Menkauhor Kaiu|WD=Q269257|lt=Menkauhor Kaiu}}''' === '''Architectural Inspiration''' === The design of '''solar temples''' follows the '''three-part layout''' of '''royal pyramid complexes''': 1. '''Valley Temple''' 2. '''Causeway''' 3. '''Upper Sanctuary on the Desert Plateau''' A '''large obelisk''' served as the '''focal point''' of the sanctuary, mirroring the '''pyramid''' in traditional '''royal complexes'''. === '''Possible Connections to Heliopolis''' === It is debated whether the '''{{ill|Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|de|Tempel des Re in Heliopolis|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}''' served as the '''prototype''' for '''solar temples'''. '''{{ill|Jochem Kahl|en|Jochem Kahl|WD=Q1691027|lt=Jochem Kahl}}''' suggests that '''{{ill|Ra|en|Ra|WD=Q1252904|lt=Ra}}''' may have been '''worshiped as early as the Second Dynasty''', though his association with '''Heliopolis''' is not firmly attested until the '''Pyramid Texts''' at the end of the '''Fifth Dynasty'''. == '''Key Structures''' == * '''Valley Temple''': Served as the '''entrance''' to the '''causeway'''. * '''Causeway''': A '''100-meter-long sloped ramp''' connecting the '''Valley Temple''' to the '''Upper Temple'''. * '''Obelisk''': The '''primary cult object''', likely '''37 meters tall'''. * '''Altar''': A '''circular alabaster slab''', surrounded by '''four hieroglyphic "ḥtp" blocks''' symbolizing '''offerings''' to '''Ra'''. * '''Great and Small Slaughterhouses''': Featured '''alabaster basins''', likely for '''ritual purification''' rather than actual '''animal slaughter'''. * '''Solar Barque''': A '''20-meter-long brick structure''', imitating the '''mythological boat of Ra'''. == '''Function and Religious Role''' == The '''temple cult''' was dedicated to '''Ra, Hathor''', and the '''Pharaoh''', with a '''priesthood''' ensuring ritual maintenance. The complex emphasized '''Ra's role as the creator''', featuring elaborate '''seasonal reliefs''' that '''depicted natural cycles''': * '''Animal reproduction''' * '''Fish migration in the Nile''' * '''Arrival of birds in the Delta''' * '''Harvesting of flax, honey, and figs''' This '''imagery reinforced the concept of eternal renewal''', both in '''nature''' and '''kingship'''. == '''Further Reading''' == {{Cite book |author={{ill|Miroslav Verner|en|Miroslav Verner|WD=Q1938506|lt=Miroslav Verner}} |title=The Pyramids: The Mystery, Culture, and Science of Egypt's Great Monuments |publisher=Rowohlt |year=1998 |ISBN=3-498-07062-2}} {{Navigation Solar Temples of the Fifth Dynasty}} [[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]] [[ar:معبد ني وسر رع]] [[arz:معبد الشمس نى-اوسر-رع]] {{Commons category|Nyuserre sun temple}} [[fr:Temple solaire d'Abou Ghorab]] [[nl:Zonnetempel van Nioeserre]] [[sk:Niuserreho slnečný chrám]] {{translated page|de|Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre|version=249954049|comment=Imported full de history}} {{wikidata link|Q2009417}} [[Category:Abusir]] [[Category:Ancient Egyptian temples]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:Pages without valid translation templates or en interwikis]] [[Category:Ra]] [[Category:Sonnenheiligtum der 5. Dynastie]] [[Category:Temples by person]] [[Category:Temples in Egypt]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

no official records exist. * '''1882/83''': '''{{ill|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|de|Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henry Windsor Villiers-Stuart|qq=|WD=Q5729559}}''' uncovered '''ten alabaster basins''' and the '''alabaster altar'''. * '''1898–1901''': '''{{ill|Ludwig Borchardt|en|Ludwig Borchardt|WD=Q60758|lt=Ludwig Borchardt}}''' and '''{{ill|Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|de|Heinrich Schäfer (Ägyptologe)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|qq=|WD=Q98050}}''' fully excavated the site on behalf of the '''{{ill|Deutsche |editor={{ill|Wolfgang Helck|en|Wolfgang Helck|WD=Q74888|lt=Wolfgang Helck}} |title=Abu-Gurab |series={{ill|Lexicon of Egyptology|de|Lexikon der Ägyptologie|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lexicon of Egyptology|qq=|WD=Q1822307}} |volume=I |publisher=Harrassowitz |location=Wiesbaden |year=1975 |ISBN=3-447-01670-1 |pages=23}} Financial support was provided by '''{{ill|Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing|en|Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing|WD=Q121278|lt=Friedrich Wilhelm von Bissing}}'''. == '''Location and Significance''' == The '''Solar Temple of Niuserre''', named '''''Šsp-jb-Rˁ''''' ("Pleasure of '''{{ill|Ra|en|Ra|WD=Q1252904|lt=Ra}}'''"), is located '''approximately 1.2 km northeast''' of the '''{{ill|Pyramids of Abusir|de|Pyramiden von Abusir|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pyramids of Abusir|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}'''. The name '''"Abusir"''' derives from the Greek '''"Busiris"''', which itself comes from the Egyptian '''"Pr Wsjr"''' ("House of Osiris"). The '''solar temple''' was constructed on a natural hill, which was further elevated using artificial embankments. Beneath the structure, remains of '''older brick buildings''', possibly '''mastabas''', have been discovered. == '''The Solar Temple Complex''' == Unlike other '''temples''' dedicated to various deities, '''solar temples''' feature '''an open courtyard''', where a '''central altar''' and '''cult object''' stand in the open air. This contrasts with traditional '''Egyptian temples''', which were designed as enclosed sanctuaries housing the '''god's image'''. === '''Known Solar Temples''' === A total of '''eight solar temples''' are known from '''historical texts''', but only '''two''' have been '''excavated''': 1. '''Niuserre's Solar Temple''' (this site) 2. '''{{ill|Sun Temple of Userkaf|en|Sun Temple of Userkaf|WD=Q2301943|lt=Solar Temple of Userkaf}}''' Other '''undiscovered''' solar temples belong to: * '''{{ill|Sahure|en|Sahure|WD=Q243692|lt=Sahure}}''' * '''{{ill|Neferirkare Kakai|en|Neferirkare Kakai|WD=Q268576|lt=Neferirkare Kakai}}''' * '''{{ill|Neferefre|en|Neferefre|WD=Q269271|lt=Raneferef}}''' * '''{{ill|Menkauhor Kaiu|en|Menkauhor Kaiu|WD=Q269257|lt=Menkauhor Kaiu}}''' === '''Architectural Inspiration''' === The design of '''solar temples''' follows the '''three-part layout''' of '''royal pyramid complexes''': 1. '''Valley Temple''' 2. '''Causeway''' 3. '''Upper Sanctuary on the Desert Plateau''' A '''large obelisk''' served as the '''focal point''' of the sanctuary, mirroring the '''pyramid''' in traditional '''royal complexes'''. === '''Possible Connections to Heliopolis''' === It is debated whether the '''{{ill|Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|de|Tempel des Re in Heliopolis|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple of Ra in Heliopolis|qq=|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work|comment=no wikipedias work}}''' served as the '''prototype''' for '''solar temples'''. The complex emphasized '''Ra's role as the creator''', featuring elaborate '''seasonal reliefs''' that '''depicted natural cycles''': * '''Animal reproduction''' * '''Fish migration in the Nile''' * '''Arrival of birds in the Delta''' * '''Harvesting of flax, honey, and figs''' This '''imagery reinforced the concept of eternal renewal''', both in '''nature''' and '''kingship'''. == '''Further Reading''' == {{Cite book |author={{ill|Miroslav Verner|en|Miroslav Verner|WD=Q1938506|lt=Miroslav Verner}} |title=The Pyramids: The Mystery, Culture, and Science of Egypt's Great Monuments |publisher=Rowohlt |year=1998 |ISBN=3-498-07062-2}} {{Navigation Solar Temples of the Fifth Dynasty}} [[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]] [[ar:معبد ني وسر رع]] [[arz:معبد الشمس نى-اوسر-رع]] {{Commons category|Nyuserre sun temple}} [[fr:Temple solaire d'Abou Ghorab]] [[nl:Zonnetempel van Nioeserre]] [[sk:Niuserreho slnečný chrám]] {{translated page|de|Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre|version=249954049|comment=Imported full de history}} {{wikidata link|Q2009417}} [[Category:Abusir]] [[Category:Ancient Egyptian temples]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Pages without valid translation templates or en interwikis]] [[Category:Ra]] [[Category:Sonnenheiligtum der 5. However, reliefs depicting a '''{{ill|Sed festival|en|Sed festival|WD=Q604644|lt=Sed festival|1=Sed festival}}''' were discovered, sparking interest in further exploration. * '''1842''': Members of '''{{ill|Karl Richard Lepsius|en|Karl Richard Lepsius|WD=Q77231|lt=Karl Richard Lepsius|1=Karl Richard Lepsius}}''', conducted precise measurements and listed the site as '''"XV"''' in the '''{{ill|Lepsius list of pyramids|en|Lepsius list of pyramids|WD=Q224877|lt=Lepsius list of pyramids|1=Lepsius list of pyramids}}'''. * '''1882''': '''{{ill|Auguste Mariette|en|Auguste '''alabaster altar'''. * '''1898–1901''': '''{{ill|Ludwig Borchardt|en|Ludwig Borchardt|WD=Q60758|lt=Ludwig Borchardt|1=Ludwig Borchardt}}''' and '''{{ill|Heinrich Schäfer (Egyptologist)|de|Heinrich The complex emphasized '''Ra's role as the creator''', featuring elaborate '''seasonal reliefs''' that '''depicted natural cycles''': * '''Animal reproduction''' * '''Fish migration in the Nile''' * '''Arrival of birds in the Delta''' * '''Harvesting of flax, honey, and figs''' This '''imagery reinforced the concept of eternal renewal''', both in '''nature''' and '''kingship'''. == '''Further Reading''' == {{Cite book |author={{ill|Miroslav Verner|en|Miroslav Verner|WD=Q1938506|lt=Miroslav Verner|1=Miroslav Verner}} |title=The Pyramids: The Mystery, Culture, and Science of Egypt's Great Monuments |publisher=Rowohlt |year=1998 |ISBN=3-498-07062-2}} {{Navigation Solar Temples of the Fifth Dynasty}} [[de:Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre]] [[ar:معبد ني وسر رع]] [[arz:معبد الشمس نى-اوسر-رع]] {{Commons category|Nyuserre sun temple}} [[fr:Temple solaire d'Abou Ghorab]] [[nl:Zonnetempel van Nioeserre]] [[sk:Niuserreho slnečný chrám]] {{translated page|de|Sonnenheiligtum des Niuserre|version=249954049|comment=Imported full de history}} {{wikidata link|Q2009417}} [[Category:Abusir]] [[Category:Ancient Egyptian temples]] [[Category:Ra]] [[Category:Sonnenheiligtum der 5.
